problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $3$rd term is $4$ and the common ratio is $2?$
worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 4 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {2}^{(3-1)} \\ 4 & =4{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=1$ and $r=2.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{1(1-{2}^{N})}{1-2} \\  & =-(1-{2}^{N}) \\  & ={2}^{N}-1\end{aligned}
$$
